blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) reason over speech, environmental sounds, music, and other acoustic information. However, their audio encoders produce dense token sequences that make long-form audio costly to process. Existing audio pruning methods reduce this cost using heuristics such as attention, representation similarity, or temporal sampling, but do not explicitly learn which tokens are most useful for a given question. We propose AudioScorer, a lightweight model that scores audio tokens according to the user question. It is trained by distilling the ranking of audio tokens under the frozen LALM's answer-gradient saliency, together with downstream answer supervision. Compared with other pruning methods, AudioScorer achieves the best or tied-best result at 10% token retention on 7 of 10 semantic and acoustic tasks, including speech recognition, emotion recognition, and audio-scene classification.
blocks.zh: 大型音频语言模型(LALMs)理性比语音,环境声音,音乐等声学信息. 然而,他们的音频编码器产生密集的符号序列,使长式音频处理成本高昂. 现有的音频冲洗方法利用注意,表现相似性,或时间采样等热力学方法来降低这一成本,但没有明确知道哪些符号对特定问题最有用. 我们提出AudioScouncer,一个轻量级的模型,根据用户的问题来评分音频符号. 它通过在被冷冻的LALM的解答分级优势下对音频符的排名进行分馏来培训,同时进行下游解答监督. 相较于其他打分方法,AudioScore器在10个语义和声学任务中的7个任务上以10%的符号保留来达到最佳或捆绑的最佳结果,包括语音识别,情感识别,和音频-场景分类.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) extend LLM reasoning to modalities such as vision and audio Alayrac et al. (2022) ; Li et al. (2023) ; Liu et al. (2023) ; OpenAI (2023) . Particularly, Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) Chu et al. (2023) ; Tang et al. (2024) ; Ghosh et al. (2026) ; Xu et al. (2025b) encode audio into dense embedding sequences projected into the LLM input space. Since the number of audio tokens grows with duration, long recordings substantially increase decoder cost. For example, Qwen2-Audio Chu et al. (2024) processes about 25 25 audio tokens
per second, yielding roughly 750 750 tokens for a 30 30 -second clip. A given
question, however, may depend on only a fraction of them, motivating
task-aware token pruning.

blocks.en:
Existing pruning methods reduce token cost in MLLMs using signals such as attention Chen et al. (2024) ; He et al. (2026) ; Zhang et al. (2025) , redundancy Wen et al. (2025) , temporal sampling He et al. (2025) , or learned relevance. Question-aware audio pruning is also established Lin et al. (2025) , while learned relevance prediction has been explored in vision Takezoe et al. (2026) . Existing question-aware pruning methods largely rely on predefined signals, while
learned relevance predictors are typically question-independent. Learning
audio-token utility jointly from the question and downstream answer quality
thus remains underexplored. This motivates our central question: Can a scoring network learn question-conditioned audio-token
relevance from signals of downstream answer utility?

blocks.en:
We introduce AudioScorer, a lightweight question-conditioned scorer trained
by distilling the frozen LALM’s gradient-based ranking of audio tokens
according to how strongly the correct answer depends on them, together with
downstream answer supervision. Figure 1 shows that AudioScorer’s token selection
changes more with the question for the same audio clip than that of the other
pruning methods. At 10 % 10\% token retention on AudioMarathon He et al. (2025) , AudioScorer is
best or tied-best on 7 7 of 10 10 tasks and leads on Speech Content, Audio
Classification, and Speaker Information. Notably, ASR reaches a 31.25 % 31.25\% word accuracy rate (WAR), compared with 5.15 % 5.15\% for the strongest baseline.
Our codebase will be released upon publication to support reproducibility.

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en: 2.1 Design Hypotheses
blocks.zh: 2.1 设计假设

blocks.en:
Our goal is to retain the audio tokens most useful for answering the user’s
question under a fixed token budget. We build AudioScorer around two
hypotheses. (H1) Token relevance depends on the question: the same audio token
may be useful for one question and irrelevant for another. (H2) The frozen LALM can serve as a relevance teacher: given the
question and reference answer, gradient-based sensitivity of the answer
likelihood provides a useful signal of audio-token relevance.

可能对一个问题有用,对另一个问题无关紧要。 (H2) 冷冻的LALM可以作为相关教师:

blocks.en:
We encode the question with bge-base-en-v1.5 Xiao et al. (2024) and use a lightweight cross-attention layer in which each audio token attends
to the question tokens. A scoring head maps the resulting
question-conditioned representation to one score per audio token, allowing
the same recording to receive different rankings for different questions.

blocks.en:
For each training example, we feed the full audio and question to the frozen
LALM, teacher-force the reference answer, and backpropagate its log-likelihood
to the audio tokens at the decoder input. Each token’s gradient norm measures
the local sensitivity of the answer to that token. We normalize these values
into soft token-level targets that supervise AudioScorer’s ranking. We
complement this with downstream answer supervision. We scale each audio token
by its predicted score: higher-scoring tokens are suppressed less than
lower-scoring tokens. At inference, soft weighting is replaced
by hard Top- K K pruning after layer ℓ p \ell_{p} . Full details are provided in
Appendix A .

blocks.en:
The benefit of AudioScorer is most pronounced on speech tasks under aggressive
compression. At 10 % 10\% retention, it improves Speech Content by 13.38 13.38 points over the strongest baseline, as shown in Table 1 . This improvement is substantially larger than those observed for Audio Classification ( 0.57 0.57 points) and Speaker Information ( 1.13 1.13 points). SpeechPrune leads on Audio Authenticity. AudioScorer is best or tied-best on seven subtasks; its Speech Content advantage includes ASR ( 31.25 31.25 versus 5.15 5.15 for HeadRouter) and SCR ( 74.57 74.57 versus 69.20 69.20 for FastV). At 40 % 40\% and 70 % 70\% , it also leads on Speech Content. On MMAU-Pro, it achieves the highest weighted score among pruning methods at all three budgets and, at 10 % 10\% retention, stays within 0.06 0.06 points of the unpruned model ( 48.51 48.51 versus 48.57 48.57 ), as shown in Table 2 . Appendix C gives all category results. Figure 3 further shows that deleting each method’s highest-ranked tokens degrades AudioScorer most on average, supporting the informativeness of its ranking. AudioScorer’s selection is relatively cheap: it adds on average 0.16 0.16 TFLOPs over Frame, which prunes at the same depth without scoring, i.e., 0.4 0.4 – 0.9 % 0.9\% of total prefilling compute as shown in Table 1 .

blocks.en: Figure 4 shows strong task-dependent sensitivity to pruning. At 10 % 10\% retention, ASR nearly collapses for most methods and SD degrades substantially, while MC, SGR, SED, and ASC remain more robust. ER is a notable exception: pruning improves it for most methods, with the largest gain for AudioScorer ( → 43.75 33.82\!\rightarrow\!43.75 ). MMAU-Pro shows a similar effect, where 40 % 40\% retention improves the weighted score from 48.57 48.57 to 49.53 49.53 . One possible explanation is that pruning filters irrelevant context and mitigates lost-in-the-middle effects Liu et al. (2024) , though our results do not establish this as the sole cause.

blocks.en: 4 Ablation Study
blocks.zh: 4 读取研究

blocks.en:
Table 3 shows that both of our supervision signals are important,
especially under aggressive pruning. Relevance distillation has the largest
effect: removing it substantially degrades Speech Content and Audio
Classification at 10 % 10\% retention. Removing downstream CE causes a
similar but smaller decline. This supports their complementary roles:
gradient-based targets provide explicit token-level relevance supervision, whereas
CE directly optimizes the retained evidence for answer quality. Simplifying the scoring head to a single
linear layer reduces Speech Content performance at 10 % 10\% retention. Replacing soft weighting with
hard Top- K K training using a straight-through estimator
(STE) Bengio et al. (2013) also hurts Speech Content and Audio
Classification at 10 % 10\% retention, while remaining competitive or slightly
better at 40 % 40\% and 70 % 70\% . This suggests that soft weighting is most helpful
when pruning is aggressive. Question cross-attention has a smaller and more task-dependent effect,
suggesting that much of the gain comes from learned relevance supervision, with
explicit question conditioning providing additional adaptation. No component is
uniformly beneficial across all categories. Full subtask results are provided in
Appendix D .

blocks.en: 5 Related Work
blocks.zh: 5 相关工作

blocks.en:
FastV Chen et al. (2024) uses attention-based
ranking, DART Wen et al. (2025) removes redundant tokens, and
AudioMarathon He et al. (2025) evaluates these methods for long audio
alongside uniform sampling. SpeechPrune Lin et al. (2025) combines speech–text similarity with approximated attention, while HeadRouter He et al. (2026) uses calibrated head profiles.
Other methods reduce tokens through merging rather than pruning Xiang et al. (2026) ; Bolya et al. (2023) . LearnPruner Takezoe et al. (2026) learns question-independent vision pruning, introducing question conditioning only later within the decoder. AudioScorer instead learns question-conditioned audio-token relevance from reference-answer gradients and downstream supervision, contributing a new supervision and pruning design for audio.

其他方法通过并购而不是由run等(2026); Bolya等(2023)来减少信使. 学普鲁纳·竹佐等. (2026)学习了问题独立视觉穿梭,只在解码器内部较后引入了问题调节. 音频 计分员转而从参考回答梯度和下游监理中学习有问题条件的音频切换相关性,为音频提供了新的监理和穿行设计.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: AudioScorer learns question-conditioned audio-token relevance using supervision from a frozen LALM. At aggressive retention budgets, it improves speech recognition, audio classification, and speaker information modeling over pruning baselines. The category-level trade-offs motivate further work on task-adaptive selection for efficient long-form audio understanding.
blocks.zh: AudioScoreer通过从被冷冻的LALM的监控中学习出问题条件的音频切换关联性. 在积极的保留预算方面,它改进了语音识别、音频分类和演讲者信息模型,超越了排出的基准。 类别层面的取舍激励进一步开展任务调整选择工作,以高效的长式音频理解.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our experiments are limited to Qwen2.5-Omni-3B and the audio modality. Moreover, performance gains are not uniform across tasks under aggressive pruning. For example, audio authenticity detection degrades substantially
at 10 % 10\% retention. Improvements over competing methods should therefore be
interpreted in the context of these task-dependent trade-offs.
blocks.zh:
我们的实验仅限于Quen2.5-Omni-3B和音频模式. 此外,在侵略性竞争下,各项任务的业绩收益并不一致。 例如,音频真实性检测可大幅降解
10%的预留额。 因此,应当改进相互竞争的方法。
结合这些取决于任务的取舍加以解释。

blocks.en:
Question conditioning yields modest and task-dependent gains in our ablations. Neither our training datasets nor the evaluation benchmarks directly target
question-specific token selection. AudioScorer is trained from individual
audio–question–answer examples, without explicit supervision that contrasts
which evidence should be selected for different questions on the same
recording. Likewise, the benchmarks evaluate downstream task performance
rather than question-dependent changes in the selected evidence. We therefore
cannot determine whether the modest gains reflect a limitation of the
conditioning mechanism or of the used evaluation.
More controlled question-switching data would allow this effect to be assessed
directly. Our evaluation is subject to benchmark limitations. To the
best of our knowledge, AudioMarathon had not been published in a
peer-reviewed venue at the time of submission.

blocks.en: Appendix A AudioScorer Architecture and Training Details
blocks.zh: 附录A 音频计分器建筑和培训细节

blocks.en: We describe the configuration of the reported Qwen2.5-Omni-3B checkpoint. The LALM, including its audio encoder, remains frozen. We train only the scorer and its question-conditioning components; the gradient teacher described below has no parameters.
blocks.zh: 我们描述了所报告的Qun2.5-Omni-3B检查站的配置。 LALM,包括其音频编码器,仍然被冻结. 我们只训练计分器及其问号组件;下文所描述的梯度老师没有参数.

blocks.en: A.1 Training Details
blocks.zh: A.1 培训细节

blocks.en:
The supervised mixture covers speech transcription, dialogue, sound description, music understanding, speaker characteristics, emotion, and audio authenticity. LibriSpeech Panayotov et al. (2015) supplies transcription and gender-label examples. MultiDialog and IEMOCAP are drawn from the LongAudio-XL resources Ghosh et al. (2026) ; Park et al. (2024) ; Busso et al. (2008) ; AudioCaps Kim et al. (2019) provides sound captions. WavText5K, YouTube-8M, and MusicBench use the AudioSkills-XL resources Ghosh et al. (2026) ; Deshmukh et al. (2023) ; Abu-El-Haija et al. (2016) ; Melechovsky et al. (2024) . Audio-authenticity examples come from the deepfake-audio-detection dataset Stafford (2024) .
We train for three epochs on a single NVIDIA A6000 GPU using
AdamW Loshchilov and Hutter (2019) with a learning rate of 10 − 4 10^{-4} .
Training AudioScorer takes approximately 9 9 GPU-hours.
To balance the training sources, we randomly sample 1,000 1{,}000 examples from each dataset without replacement using a fixed seed of 42 42 . The selected subsets remain fixed across epochs. Final evaluation uses the available 6,347 6{,}347 AudioMarathon and 5,305 5{,}305 MMAU-Pro examples.

blocks.en: Appendix B SpeechPrune Baseline Implementation

blocks.en:
We reimplement SpeechPrune Lin et al. (2025) while preserving its
training-free, two-stage selection procedure. The first stage ranks
temporal audio groups using speech–question cosine similarity, while the
second stage further filters the retained representation using
first-layer attention.

ASR is particularly sensitive to the training objectives under aggressive pruning. At 10 % 10\% retention, removing relevance distillation reduces ASR from 31.25 31.25 to 0.00 0.00 ; removing downstream CE, using a linear scoring head,

SCR is more robust, although removing distillation or using STE still
lowers performance. Removing question cross-attention reduces ASR and
SER by approximately 3 3 points each while slightly improving SCR.
At larger budgets, most variants retain near-unpruned ASR performance,
indicating that these differences matter most under severe compression.
